summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, secondary adrenal insufficiency, morbid obesity, and prior pulmonary embolism was admitted for syncope and dizziness. He had been experiencing orthostatic symptoms and an episode of fainting after standing, prompting evaluation for cardiac, metabolic, and neurologic causes. Workup revealed a subtherapeutic INR, which was corrected with warfarin dose adjustment and bridging anticoagulation. Cardiac testing, including a nuclear stress test and echocardiogram, showed no evidence of ischemia or significant dysfunction, though image quality was limited by body habitus. His chronic bilateral parotid and submandibular gland enlargement, consistent with fatty infiltration and sialadenitis, remained stable on imaging with no signs of infection or malignancy. LDH was markedly elevated without clear etiology, prompting further outpatient evaluation. Diuretics were held due to persistent dizziness, with furosemide restarted before discharge while spironolactone and HCTZ were discontinued. He was discharged to extended care with plans for outpatient ENT, neurology, and cardiology follow-up, along with monitoring of INR, electrolytes, and pending AFP results.
problems: Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
